title: Predicting Post-Therapeutic Visual Acuity and OCT Images in Patients With Central Serous Chorioretinopathy by Artificial Intelligence
summary: Learned prognosis models predict post-laser acuity and OCT against observed outcomes, including a separate-center test cohort; this does not establish treatment benefit. Training/validation at ZOC and independent XEC test cohort; comparison with ground-truth and specialist assessments.
ai_technology: Blended regressors forecast post-laser visual acuity; pix2pixHD generates later OCT from pretreatment scans.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Retrospective cohort results compare predicted visual acuity and synthetic OCT with measured outcomes; this is prognostic prediction, not treatment benefit.
evidence.unknown: Training/validation at ZOC and independent XEC test cohort; comparison with ground-truth and specialist assessments. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Blended regressors forecast post-laser visual acuity; pix2pixHD generates later OCT from pretreatment scans.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
